The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the emotional arc of the narrative. The first three sections of the story stretch out a single Saturday visit from 8:15 AM to 4:00 PM. This slower pacing mirrors the unhurried, static nature of the mother’s life in Orosi and allows the writer to establish the intricate details of their relationship—as well as the specific objects (the crossword, the water glass, the score sheet, the straw hat) that will become emotionally resonant later. 

Then, the author sharply compresses time, skipping ahead "five weeks later" in a single transition, and condensing four days in the ICU into a single short paragraph. This rapid compression reflects the sudden, jarring nature of a medical emergency and the disorienting speed at which an aging parent's independence can vanish. Finally, the story slows down again in the last section as the narrator returns to the empty house. This deceleration allows the reader to sit with the narrator's grief and realization, giving weight to the small details left behind from that stretched-out Saturday five weeks prior.
